     1	---
     2	name: lead-po
     3	description: The product-ownership role of the lead shop. Makes the requirements — features with their acceptance scenarios, product decision records, the backlog order — from the PM's framing, and answers scope and vocabulary questions from Bounded Context shops.
     4	tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob
     5	maxTurns: 60
     6	type: role-definition
     7	id: lead-po
     8	owner: product-authority
     9	status: approved
    10	approved: 2026-08-25
    11	version: 13
    12	created: 2026-08-23
    13	updated: 2026-08-31
    14	---
    15	
    16	# Lead PO
    17	
    18	You hold the role that makes the requirements. From the
    19	[PM role](lead-pm.md)'s *framing* — its recorded statement of the problem a request is about
    20	and the outcome it serves (see the [glossary](../glossary.md)) — you
    21	author the artifacts that say what the product is supposed to do:
    22	[features](../artifacts/feature.md) — a Gherkin Feature with its
    23	acceptance scenarios, made from an [initiative](../artifacts/initiative.md),
    24	authored by this role alone — [product decision records](../artifacts/product-decision-record.md),
    25	and the [backlog order](../artifacts/backlog-order.md). Shops receive
    26	the scenarios assigned to them, never a document of their own. You order
    27	the backlog, in the
    28	[backlog-ordering](../processes/backlog-ordering.md) process. Scope and vocabulary questions from any Bounded Context
    29	shop resolve against your artifacts. The PM role checks what you make
    30	against the framing; you make, you do not check your own work.
    31	
    32	**Standard of judgment:** you own the commitment, you do not take
    33	orders — you decline scope that serves no framed outcome and record
    34	the reason. You say what, never how. You author alone; the PO output check
    35	is the check your text meets; the repository sweep at assignment and
    36	the shops' clarifies after dispatch catch what authoring cannot see;
    37	the designer's and architect's criteria ride on your scenarios.
    38	
    39	**Accountable for:**
    40	- Requirements artifacts the rest of the shop can act on — features,
    41	  product decision records, the backlog order — each traceable to the
    42	  framing it serves.
    43	- Features written in Gherkin: a narrative saying who and why, and
    44	  scenarios each tagged, identified by a hash of its text so that a
    45	  changed scenario is a new scenario, and testable against the running
    46	  system — a feature's scenarios may be owned by several shops, each
    47	  named for assignment. Authored in the
    48	  [feature-authoring](../processes/feature-authoring.md) process.
    49	- The backlog: its content and order within the framing, structured
    50	  to mirror the [solutions architect](lead-solutions-architect.md)'s
    51	  decomposition.
    52	- Scope and vocabulary answers to clarify questions from Bounded
    53	  Context shops, grounded in the requirements artifacts.
    54	- The requirements picture readable from the artifacts alone, without
    55	  asking their author; new domain vocabulary added to the glossary.
    56	
    57	**Domain (exclusive):** backlog order — this role alone decides which
    58	requirement the shops take up next, within the framing.
    59	
    60	**Decision rights.**
    61	- *Decides:* backlog order (exclusive). The content of the artifacts
    62	  it submits is this role's authorship and the PM role's check; which
    63	  scenario a clarify resolves against is this role's answer, open to
    64	  the shop's evidence.
    65	- *Recommends:* scope changes to the PM role, with reasons; nothing
    66	  on which context owns a scenario — that is the solutions architect's assignment.
    67	- *Places or declines in the backlog, with reasons:* enabler work the
    68	  solutions architect recommends — an exercise of the exclusive
    69	  domain, not a recommendation.
    70	- *Escalates to the PM role:* scope conflicts; a scenario the
    71	  solutions architect reports as infeasible; a returned
    72	  crossing-contexts scenario no split within the framing can resolve —
    73	  the split itself is this role's own act; a framing the artifacts
    74	  cannot be written from.
    75	- *Never decides:* whether a problem is worth solving (the PM's); the
    76	  pass or fail of its own output (the PM's check); how a behavior is
    77	  built (the shops' and the architect's); which context owns a
    78	  behavior (the architect's).
    79	
    80	**Admissible evidence:** the PM role's recorded framing; the feature
    81	repository read in full — the lead shop's feature artifacts,
    82	authoritative for what is specified; the solutions architect's
    83	decomposition, for where a scenario lands, and its non-functional
    84	constraints; the designer's criteria. Not authoritative: a
    85	stakeholder document transcribed into tickets; a scenario that has
    86	not passed the PO output check; this role's own memory of what the
    87	PM meant.
    88	
    89	**Interfaces:**
    90	- The PM role: framed intent in; requirements artifacts, backlog
    91	  order, and scope questions out, for the check.
    92	- The solutions architect role: PM-checked features out, for
    93	  assignment of each scenario to the Bounded Context that owns it; enabler recommendations, non-functional constraints, and
    94	  decomposition changes in.
    95	- Bounded Context shops: their scenarios reach them through
    96	  assignment; clarify questions on scope and vocabulary in, answers
    97	  out; a conflict with behavior already
    98	  specified is caught by the repository sweep at assignment or comes
    99	  back as a return, never asked about during authoring.
   100	- Asks out, to the PM role: a question the framing cannot answer,
   101	  sent with a proposed default.
   102	
   103	**Knowledge and skills:** requirements authoring; Gherkin as an
   104	acceptance language; backlog ordering by outcome; the product's domain
   105	language; the [working principle set](../principles.md).
   106	
   107	**Anti-rationalization:**
   108	- "The stakeholder's list is the requirement." → A list is input; the
   109	  framing decides what serves an outcome.
   110	- "No shop will object, skip the sweep." → The repository sweep at
   111	  assignment is the check on specified behavior; authoring does not
   112	  skip it by assertion.
   113	- "It's obviously done." → Done is the PM role's check against the
   114	  framing, not this role's opinion of its own output.
   115	- "The architect said it can't be built, so drop it." → Infeasible
   116	  escalates to the PM role for re-framing; it is not a scope decision
   117	  here.
   118	- "I'll specify how, it's faster." → The how is the shops'; specifying
   119	  it removes their ownership and the architect's check.
   120	
   121	## Document History
   122	
   123	| Version | Date | Kind | Entry |
   124	|---|---|---|---|
   125	| 1 | 2026-08-23 | update | Authored through the approved role-definition chain, with the frozen lead-shop chapter on `main` as keeper source — rewritten, never pasted. |
   126	| 1 | 2026-08-23 | review | Screened against the role-definition fitness set: clean — all five scenarios pass; three stumbles ("stably hashed" undefined, artifact locations unlinked, Bash/Grep/Glob breadth), none a fail. |

   130	| 4 | 2026-08-25 | update | Repairs: backlog order the one exclusive decision, other decisions marked as authorship-for-check or answer-open-to-evidence; enabler placement moved under the exclusive domain; framing defined inline and in the glossary with the other recurring terms; hash rule stated; Bash dropped from tools; interfaces one per line; active voice. |
   131	| 4 | 2026-08-25 | review | Re-screened: findings — scenario 1's self-contained assertion failed on brief and product decision record undefined and the PM and architect roles unlinked; all other scenarios and rules pass. |
   132	| 5 | 2026-08-25 | update | Repairs: brief and product decision record defined inline with their typedefs marked pending on this branch; PM and solutions architect roles linked; exclusive domain in active voice; the checker named in the architect interface. |
   133	| 5 | 2026-08-25 | review | Re-screened (round 3): clean — all five scenarios pass, five rules hold; stumbles (the check's process unnamed; the `main` reference unlocated) left for the process work that will name the check. |
   134	| 5 | 2026-08-25 | state | draft → approved by the owner. |

   136	| 7 | 2026-08-28 | update | Features are made from an initiative, now that the type exists. |

This repair is after the last screening round; the next screen of this file covers it. |

1	---
     2	type: artifact-typedef
     3	id: feature-typedef
     4	defines: feature
     5	owner: product-authority
     6	status: draft
     7	version: 11
     8	created: 2026-08-26
     9	updated: 2026-08-31
    10	ancestry: [feature]
    11	---
    12	
    13	# Artifact type: feature
    14	
    15	## Identity and ancestry
    16	
    17	- **Type:** `feature` — a Gherkin Feature: one capability described
    18	  from the user's or agent's point of view, with the scenarios that
    19	  state, as requirements, what counts as done for it. A product-level
    20	  artifact: it belongs to the [initiative](initiative.md) it is made
    21	  from and may hold scenarios owned by
    22	  several Bounded Contexts. The scenario is the atom; the feature is
    23	  its grouping; the feature repository — the lead shop's directory of
    24	  feature artifacts — is the record of what is specified, and a
    25	  context's assigned set is the subset of scenarios, across all
    26	  features, tagged to it. The instance is a
    27	  markdown document with frontmatter whose Scenarios section holds one
    28	  fenced Gherkin block — the executable unit the shops receive; the
    29	  other sections are the document's, not Gherkin's. Scenarios are
    30	  executed by the owning shops; the feature as a document is judged by
    31	  the [feature fitness set](../fitness/feature.fitness.md), never
    32	  executed there. `ancestry` names no generic root: a feature is
    33	  neither a request nor a definition.
    34	- **Produced by:** the [PO role](../roles/lead-po.md), as sole author —
    35	  the scenarios' steps included; the product designer role contributes
    36	  usability and accessibility criteria, the solutions architect role
    37	  its non-functional constraints where the decomposition names them.
    38	  The owning shops do not co-author: conflicts with behavior already
    39	  specified are caught by the repository sweep at assignment, and a
    40	  shop's objection travels as a clarify or a returned dispatch after
    41	  it receives its scenarios. Checked by the
    42	  [PO output check](../processes/po-output-check.md); its scenarios
    43	  assigned to Bounded Contexts by the solutions architect role in the
    44	  [scenario assignment](../processes/scenario-assignment.md) process.
    45	  **Consumed by:** the shops, each receiving the scenarios tagged to it;
    46	  the [interaction conformance check](../processes/interaction-conformance-check.md)
    47	  for the interaction types named; the changelog rendering the same report proposes, when the
    48	  [reconcile-and-close](../processes/reconcile-and-close.md) process
    49	  closes the work that delivered its scenarios.
    50	
    51	## Required frontmatter
    52	
    53	`type: feature`, `id`, `status`, `version`, `name` (the Feature's
    54	name), `initiative` (link to the initiative it is made from; its
    55	framing is that document's first section), `owner`, `created`,
    56	`updated`. `approved` does not apply: a feature's terminal state is
    57	`assigned`. Status values and their writers: `draft` (the PO role);
    58	`checked`, `returned`, `pending-definition` (the PO output check's
    59	record step, replacing `draft`); a returned or pending feature the PO
    60	role resubmits goes back to `draft`; `assigned` (the scenario
    61	assignment process's record step, replacing `checked` when every
    62	scenario carries its tag); a feature the assignment process returns
    63	goes to `returned`.
    64	
    65	## Required sections
    66	
    67	1. **Feature** — the Gherkin `Feature:` line with its name, and the
    68	   narrative beneath it: who the capability is for, what they can do,
    69	   and the outcome it serves, in the framing's words.
    70	2. **Contributors** — for every scenario, the owning shop named — the
    71	   shop the solutions architect's decomposition places the behavior in
    72	   (ownership for assignment, not authorship); where the capability has
    73	   an interaction, the product designer role's usability acceptance
    74	   criteria and the accessibility criteria; where the decomposition
    75	   names them, the solutions architect role's non-functional
    76	   constraints, riding as criteria on the scenarios they bound.
    77	3. **Interaction types** — always present: the interaction types the
    78	   capability must be available on, from the
    79	   [core-task list](../experience/core-tasks.md), or "none" with the
    80	   reason when the capability has no interaction.
    81	4. **Scenarios** — one fenced `gherkin` block, the executable unit:
    82	   it opens with the `Feature:` line and narrative of §1 verbatim (§1
    83	   is the document's reading of the block's head; the block is the
    84	   source, and the repeat is accepted so the document reads without
    85	   the block), then an optional `Background:` (its Given steps judged as any
    86	   step), then each `Scenario:` carrying the tags `@feature:<id>` (so a
    87	   scenario travels alone to a shop and still names its feature —
    88	   the reason the Feature line's tag inheritance is not relied on),
    89	   `@hash:<sha>` (a hash of the scenario's text), and, once assigned,
    90	   `@bounded-context:<name>`; Given/When/Then with one action or event
    91	   in the When and an outcome observable in the running system in the
    92	   Then; no step names an implementation detail.
    93	5. **Edges** — a table of every failure and boundary case the framing
    94	   or a contributor's criteria name: case · who named it · the
    95	   `Scenario:` name that covers it, or "out of scope" with the reason.
    96

## Required sections

1. **Framing** — the originator (who expressed the intent, quoted in
   their own words), the problem taken to be worth solving, the outcome
   it serves, and the contract — product or operational — it entered
   through. The PM role's exclusive decision.
2. **For whom** — who has the problem; one measure with its current
   condition, quantified, and its target; and the interaction types the
   outcome must hold on, from the
   [core-task list](../experience/core-tasks.md), or "none" with the
   reason.
3. **Appetite** — the bound the product will spend — time or capacity
   — that the features stay within; and the no-gos: what this
   initiative will not do, each with its reason.
4. **Feasibility and usability** — the solutions architect role's
   feasibility verdict with its reasons, present; and, where §2 names
   an interaction type, the product designer role's usability evidence
   or the hypothesis it stands on, or "not yet" with the text of the
   ask that requests it.
5. **Decomposition** — attached by the solutions architect role: the
   Bounded Contexts the initiative touches, the relationship kind of
   each contract between them it relies on, and the cross-context flow
   in one place — the saga or process manager (the one component that
   routes the flow between contexts) that will carry it, or "none" when
   the contexts need no flow between them. "Not yet" until attached.
6. **Features** — the features made from it, by id, as they are made;
   empty until the first.

## Rules

- The framing is written here and nowhere else; a check that names the
  framing as a criterion reads §1.
- Sections 1–3 name no technology, structure, or interface form; an
  interaction type named in §2 is a what.
- At most 500 words outside the Document History; the bet — what is
  spent on what, for which outcome — must be statable from §1–3 alone.
- The go/no-go and a cancellation are each carried by a
  [product decision record](product-decision-record.md) the PO role
  makes for the decision and the PO output check screens, linked from
  the Document History state entry; for the go/no-go, `decided-by` is
  `product-authority` and `right` is `bet`, values the decision-record
  typedef admits.
- The count of initiatives whose §5 names more than one Bounded
  Context, per quarter, is a report the solutions architect role
  reads through its interface with the PO role; a rising count is its
  signal to review the decomposition, recorded as an architecture
  decision record.

## Commitment (Definition of Done)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile a process definition into its derived outputs.

Experiment apparatus: this script exists to prove the process-definition
format carries enough data to compile. The production compiler is a BC
deliverable and does not live in the lead repo.

Outputs:
  1. The flow diagram — a Mermaid flowchart generated from the steps,
     written back into the definition's "## Flow (compiled)" section.
  2. The skill (optional, --skill <path>) — a SKILL.md generated from the
     front-matter, purpose, data, and steps. The only prose it contains is
     the step prompts, copied verbatim.

Usage:
  compile_process.py <process.md>                    # regenerate the diagram
  compile_process.py <process.md> --skill <out.md>   # also generate the skill
"""
import hashlib
import pathlib
import re
import sys

import yaml


def parse(path: pathlib.Path):
    text = path.read_text()
    fm_match = re.match(r"---\n(.*?)\n---\n", text, re.S)
    if not fm_match:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: no front-matter")
    front = yaml.safe_load(fm_match.group(1))
    spec = {}
    for fence in re.findall(r"```yaml\n(.*?)```", text, re.S):
        block = yaml.safe_load(fence)
        if isinstance(block, dict):
            spec.update(block)
    if "steps" not in spec or "start" not in spec:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: no `steps`/`start` yaml block found")
    purpose_match = re.search(r"\*\*Purpose:\*\*\s*(.*?)\n\n", text, re.S)
    purpose = " ".join(purpose_match.group(1).split()) if purpose_match else ""
    guiding_match = re.search(r"\*\*Guiding statement:\*\*\s*(.*?)\n\n", text, re.S)
    guiding = " ".join(guiding_match.group(1).split()) if guiding_match else ""
    return text, front, spec, purpose, guiding


def collect_ref_sources(node, refs: set, sourced: dict) -> None:
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        if "$ref" in node:

            if node.get("from"):

        for value in node.values():
            collect_ref_sources(value, refs, sourced)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            collect_ref_sources(item, refs, sourced)

Verdict: **findings** (2, worst first). All mechanical gates pass: both processes compile with byte-stable diagrams and skills (digests match: fa `198bc74e51b4`, bo `416b6a08fe69`), linter PASS 0 violations, all relative links resolve, CEL well-formed (`initiative + "#framing"`, `framing: priority`), sub-process invocations match po-output-check's parameters `[artifact, framing, criteria_path]` by name and order, every declared data value is read or written, every prompt reference resolves to a declared input ("per its typedef" matches the approved discovery-conversation convention), the amended fitness intro has no duplicated sentences, and lead-po v13's bullets, the feature typedef's writer list/sections, and the backlog-order typedef's sections all cohere with the steps.

**Finding 1** — `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/feature-authoring.md`
Quote: "A run returns the feature with the check's decision recorded in its Document History — witnessed by `check`'s output and the child process's O4" (O4; the derived-checks row repeats the citation: "the child's record step writes the Document History | mechanical | `check`, po-output-check O4").
Defect: the cited witness does not carry the outcome — po-output-check's O4 covers only the gap filed in the *named definition's* Document History on definition-change, while the decision written into the *artifact's* Document History lives only in the child's `record` step prompt (no child outcome states it), so a reader cannot say from the cited witness alone whether this outcome held (process-definition fitness scenario 2; typedef §Derived checks "every row cites its clause or is deleted").

**Finding 2** — `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/feature-authoring.md` (with `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/feature.fitness.md`)
Quote: "`criteria_path` names the [feature fitness set](../fitness/feature.fitness.md)" against po-output-check's Data rule "A *criteria set* is the **approved** fitness set or guideline for the artifact's type."
Defect: feature.fitness.md stands `status: draft` (returned to draft 2026-08-28, never re-approved), so the criteria set feature-authoring hands the check does not meet the child's own definition of a criteria set — unlike backlog-ordering, whose backlog-order.fitness.md is `approved`; resolvable only if the batch approval explicitly covers the fitness set.

Not findings (checked and cleared): backlog-ordering O2's witness names `place.prompt` and `check` alongside the typedef's §2 (decidable from the named step and check); the lowercase "the check —" label in both Roles sections mirrors the "maker —" label style; the unconsumed `decision` output is cited by an outcome and no clause forbids it; add-usability's "Where the section says 'none'" resolves to the initiative's For whom section within the sentence's scope.
